argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The supportable position is narrower than a clean compliance claim: the admissible record supports certification only as a constrained business judgment based on aggregate readiness clearing threshold, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and governance principles that allow managed residual risk with documentation and monitoring. It does not support the broader claim that certification without a material weakness disclosure is cleanly established under policy, because the same record shows an unresolved 1.1 percentage point miss in a named launch use case, an open legal review, and no approved risk acceptance in evidence. The appropriate treatment is to distinguish weak but non-frivolous support for certification from a clean policy showing.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against treating this as clean compliance. On the admissible record, a weakness affecting a named launch use case is material unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the use case is named or legal review is pending. Aggregate readiness and general governance frameworks can support a monitored launch rationale, but they do not substitute for the policy predicate on disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost exists because delay affects the partner launch path, but business cost should not be used to restate unresolved policy predicates as satisfied. The admissible basis is only that aggregate readiness passed and the affected segment was characterized as 7% of projected first-month traffic, which may support prioritization and monitoring but not a stronger no-disclosure conclusion.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean compliant certification finding against the disclosure question.
The 7% traffic figure is not enough on this record to defeat materiality for a named launch use case.
General governance guidance does not override the internal disclosure policy.
The open legal review materially weakens any assertion that the no-disclosure posture is already settled.
No approved risk-acceptance record is identified in the admissible evidence.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence or side-channel material is offered. Private context was not relied on as public support.
